Incident Type: UNKNOWN SHEEN
Material: UNKNOWN OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 28.935833, -88.970000 (Explicit)
Report Description
***MARINE POLLUTION SURVEILLANCE REPORT*** A VERY LARGE AREA OF SUSPECTED OIL CAN BE SEEN EXTENDING SOUTHWEST FROM THE DESTROYED TAYLOR PLATFORM. THIS AREA OF SUSPECTED OIL IS JUST UNDER 50 MILES IN LENGTH BUT IS BROKEN INTO MULTIPLE SEGMENTS. THE LARGEST SEGMENT, WHICH EXTENDS 22 MILES TO THE WEST-SOUTHWEST, HAS A SILVERY APPEARANCE ALONG THE SOUTHERN EDGE OF THE SLICK AND FEATHERS OUT TO THE NORTH AND NORTHWEST. THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE EAAST-NORTHEAST SURFACE WINDS AS WELL AS THE NORTHEASTERLY OCEAN CURRENTS AROUND THE TIME OF THE IMAGE. THE SLICK THEN TURNS TO THE NORTHWEST IN A COUNTER-CLOCKWISE FASHION BUT IS BROKEN INTO MULTIPLE SEGMENTS, LIKELY DUE TO THE NORTHEASTERLY WINDS ACTING AGAINST THE SLICK AND THE OILS LONGEVITY IN THE WATER.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 36.298677, -92.280665 (Approximated from street_address)
Report Description///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1340524/// CALLER REPORTS A VESSEL AT THE MARINA EXPERIENCED AN UNSPECIFIED EQUIPMENT FAILURE, WHICH LED TO A SUDDEN FIRE. THIS SPREAD TO THE DOCK AND 14 OTHER VESSELS, ALL OF WHICH SANK. 7 OTHER VESSELS WERE SET ADRIFT BY THE FIRE, BUT HAVE SINCE BETWEEN TOWED BACK TO THE SHORE PRIOR TO SINKING. THERE IS A SMALL AMOUNT OF RAINBOW SHEENING PRESENT AROUND FLOATING DEBRIS. HOWEVER, DUE TO THE LACK OF LARGE SHEENING, IT IS EXPECTED THAT MOST OF THE FUEL ONBOARD THE VESSELS LIKELY BURNED IN THE FIRE. AN OCCUPANT OF THE VESSEL THAT CAUSED THE FIRE WENT TO THE HOSPITAL WITH SECOND DEGREE BURNS. A FIREFIGHTER ALSO WENT TO THE HOSPITAL WITH CHEST PAINS. DESCRIPTION FOR NRC REPORT #1340524: CALLER IS REPORTING A VESSEL THAT CAUGHT FIRE AT THE MARINA AND THE FIRE SPREADED ALL AROUND THE DOCK AREA. THE CALLER STATED THAT IT IS DARK SO THERE IS VERY LITTLE INFORMATION. THE CALLER STATED THAT THEY WILL CALL BACK IN THE MORNING WHEN THEY CAN SEE BETTER WITH SUNLIGHT.

THE OIL SLICK IS DESCRIBED AS LONG STRIPS (~20' WIDE X 2-5 MILES LONG) WITH WHITE FOAM ON TOP; THE FOAM DISSIPATES LEAVING A SMOOTH OIL-LIKE SURFACE THAT MAINTAINS THE COLOR OF THE WATER (I.E. USCG AUXILIARY AIRCRAFT REPORTEDLY EVALUATED SCENE BY FLYOVER. MI-DEQ STAFF RECOMMEND EVALUATION BY VESSEL AND/OR FROM LAND BY FOOT. CALLER INDICATES THAT IT IS MORE DIFFICULT TO SEE AT NIGHT. MI-DEQ STAFF REQUEST FOLLOW-UP FROM USCG STAFF.
